newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH '98 PAY AND TAX DECISIONS AT SAME TIME - TT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH '98 PAY AND TAX DECISIONS AT SAME TIME - TT.

text.p: Decisions on nominal pay rises and income tax cuts for 1998 must probably be made at the same time, Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) director-general Johannes Koroma said on Monday.

"The government has signalled ... that the pay agreements would be made first and that the possible size of tax cuts would be considered only after that," Koroma told a seminar according to the text of a prepared speech.
"From an economic policy point of view this kind of thinking is justified. What is right according to economic theory is not, however, practically possible for the labour markets," he said.
"Even this government's credibility is not so spotless in the eyes of the trade unions that vague promises of tax cuts attached to a moderate incomes settlememt would be convincing," Koroma said.
"It will be difficult to avoid simultaneous negotiations on wages and tax measures," he added.
The current two-year incomes settlement expires early in 1998 and Koroma said the decisive round of pay talks would be held around late January-early February next year.
At that time, the 1998 state budget would already have been approved by parliament and any tax changes would be known.
Income tax cuts should be targetted so that all wage earner groups stood to gain, otherwise the prospects of a moderate incomes settlement would suffer, Koroma said.

TT proposed a four billion markka income tax cut for 1998, he said, adding such a programme would provide workers with a real earnings increase equivalent to six billion markka worth of nominal pay rises.
Low-wage earners should get bigger tax cuts than others, Koroma said, adding, however, that TT aimed for lower income taxes across the board.
Tax cuts should not be financed with more state borrowing.
TT aslso opposed the financing of income tax cuts with higher energy taxation.
The shortfall in public sector tax revenues should be covered by dynamic growth effects and expendiuture savings.

"The most significant component of the budget deficit is unemployment and the costs of it," Koroma said, adding that the best solution would be that reduced unemployment would offset the shortfall in tax revenue from lower income taxes. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
